# Thesis Development

⚠️ **Finance warning / Avertissement finance** : informational only, not investment advice. A written thesis disciplines judgement, it does not make an investment safe: private equity carries a real risk of loss, and no thesis document here is a promise of return. Curated by Skill Harbor: the thesis development skill of the private equity pack in andreworia/claude-finance-skills. Use it before a market map exists and long before a target is named, when the partnership likes a sector but has no written claim anyone can argue with, or when a thesis has drifted into defending consecutive passes. The method starts by drawing the sub-sector boundary as an inclusion test precise enough that a company is either in or out (activity, customer, geography, size band), then writes the core claim in one falsifiable sentence in the form because a structural condition, a type of asset will reach a measurable outcome over a period, and names the observation that would make it false. It locates the return inside the EBITDA bridge (organic growth, margin expansion, buy-and-build arbitrage, deleveraging, exit multiple change), states which component carries most of it, and holds the exit flat to entry, labelling any expansion as upside rather than base case. It then establishes why now, a catalyst that makes this a 24-month window (a compliance date, a cost curve crossing, a cohort of sponsor-owned assets entering hold years four to six), writes three to five must-be-true conditions, each...
